A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dimension-free federated learning work, renamed from FedDisco to DeComFL. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original MNIST and Fashion-MNIST experiments in Figures 2–3 and OPT-125M fine-tuning results on SST-2 and CB in Table 2.

after.justification: v3 reports original image-classification experiments, six-task fine-tuning results for two OPT sizes in Table 2, and LoRA experiments in Appendix B.2/Table 5.

M1.justification: The shared-seed/scalar algorithm remains. The reset procedure promoted into v3's main algorithm already appeared in v2 Section 2.2. Limited extensions include the evaluated LoRA adaptation and an option for clients to maintain and transmit their participation records, described in Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: Both retain MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, SST-2, and CB. v3 adds actual evaluations on WSC, WIC, RTE, and BoolQ, substantially broadening NLP coverage to include commonsense reasoning, word-sense disambiguation, and question answering.

E2.justification: For the retained LLM tasks, Table 2 replaces the SGD comparator with FedZO at P=5 while retaining MeZO. The image experiments retain FedAvg, FedCom, and FedAvg+TopK. Extending these comparators to additional tasks does not independently change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The image-data partition description changes from even partitioning to Dirichlet alpha=1; this does not establish that the retained plots were rerun. LLM participation changes from 2 of 3 clients to 2 of 8. OPT-125M SST-2 changes from 10,000 rounds at 1e-6 to 3,000 at 5e-6, and CB from 4,000 at 1e-7 to 1,000 at 2e-6. OPT-1.3B and LoRA configurations are also added.

E4.justification: The local-step and perturbation analyses in Figures 2–3 remain. Appendix B.2/Table 5 adds a LoRA compatibility study examining performance when fewer parameters are tuned. Its learning rates and budgets differ from full-parameter tuning, so it is supplementary evidence rather than a controlled isolation of LoRA's effect.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 2's mean/standard-deviation displays and report point estimates in fine-tuning tables. v3 adds no experimental replication counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the original fine-tuning results, removes P=1 entries, and adds four tasks, OPT-1.3B results, and communication totals in bytes. For example, OPT-125M SST-2 at P=10 changes from 86.73% to 85.08%, but under changed settings, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Appendix Table 5 adds LoRA outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 substantially revises the low-rank proof: it introduces a linearized estimator and bounded finite-difference remainder, corrects the heterogeneity-covariance sign, and develops descent using the original loss. Theorem 2 tightens the step-size restriction by a factor of four and changes the smoothing-parameter condition and residual terms. The leading asymptotic rate and standard convergence theorem remain.

C1.justification: The central claims of dimension-free per-round communication and low-rank convergence remain. v3 adds a specific headline claim that billion-parameter fine-tuning needs only around 1 MB of total client–server communication, extending v2's more general empirical savings claim.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly identifies unaddressed data heterogeneity as a limitation, interprets convergence on larger models as support for low effective rank, and discusses the limited performance benefit of tuning fewer parameters through LoRA. The earlier computational-cost limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1/Table 4 adds systematic fine-tuning configuration information, including task/model learning rates and budgets, smoothing parameter 1e-3, K=1, and train/test batch sizes 32/64. Optimizer-state handling receives additional explanation. Conversely, v2's explicit project-code availability statement and link are absent from v3; this establishes removed access information, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting references on Hessian structure, CocktailSGD, SPSA, SCAFFOLD, and the additional NLP and PEFT settings, while removing the ZOO attack and multitask prompted-training citations. Its central positioning relative to MeZO, FedZO, and BAFFLE remains.

P1.justification: The method narrative is extensively rewritten around preliminaries, uplink communication, downlink reconstruction, and the complete algorithm. Related work becomes a separate section; implementation variants move into Appendix A, experiment details occupy Appendix B, and proofs become Appendix C. The algorithm is renamed throughout.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1, splits the combined pseudocode into server/client algorithms, substantially restructures Table 2 by model and dataset, and adds Tables 4–5 and a FedCom row to Table 1. Larger typography and redistribution of figures and tables change the layout extensively; Figures 2–3 largely retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the algorithm explanation, repairs identifiable steps in the low-rank derivation, and provides broader LLM validation with more explicit settings. These gains are qualified by removal of the code link and inconsistent new communication figures: Table 2 reports 0.90 MB for OPT-1.3B/P=5 on 1,500-round RTE versus 0.12 MB on 2,000-round SST-2 under the shared communication settings in Appendix B.1. Such discrepancies weaken the central quantitative evidence and limit the overall improvement.
